issues.detail: The Hebrew 'מְחַץ מָתְנַיִם קָמָיו' is an imperative (crush the loins of his adversaries), but the Chinese renders it as a wish/relative clause '願那擊打祂敵人腰間的' (may the one who strikes the loins of his enemies), changing the subject and making it a blessing on a person rather than a direct action by God. This alters who is doing the action.
